finance_aml.gbm.baseline_gap_note: Minority-class F1 0.1519 against the published 0.6323. Round 24 measured the causes rather than assuming them, and then closed the one that was actionable. RULED OUT: the decision threshold (0.6323 needs AUPRC >= ~0.40, so it is unreachable at any threshold - a ranking gap, not a tuning gap) and accounts unseen in the training window (0.39% of test rows). RULED OUT as a main cause: the 4-hop reachability limit against the corpus's 10-hop CYCLE attempts - the Graph Feature Preprocessor paper (arXiv:2402.08593) caps the multi-hop cycle and scatter-gather contribution at 'up to 4%' relative while attributing 'more than 30%' to fan-in/fan-out, which this project already implements. FIXED: the per-account aggregates were fitted with a groupby over the whole training window, so a training row's feature included its own future (median transaction had only 46.4% of its out-degree accrued by its own timestamp) while test rows got the same table as a stale past - the booster was fitted on one distribution and scored on another. Prior-at-time aggregates removed the asymmetry and lifted minority-class F1 from 0.0808 to 0.1519 (+88%), AUPRC 0.0732 to 0.1233 (+68%), AUROC 0.8980 to 0.9526, with NO leakage - verified by truncation, every causal feature being bit-identical whether or not later rows exist. WHAT REMAINS: IBM's Graph Feature Preprocessor ships in snapml under a Proprietary licence and is excluded by this project's commercial-OK-only rule; the mechanism that matters is architectural rather than legal - GFP computes per-transaction subgraph patterns over a graph updated as each transaction arrives, whereas this pipeline computes per-account scalars plus training-window structural features. Full workings: references/finance-gap-investigation.md. Reported as measured; not adjusted to close the gap.

satellite_comms.telemanom.dataset: ESA Anomaly Dataset (ESA-ADB), Mission1 lightweight channels 41-46
satellite_comms.telemanom.metric_note: Event-wise F-beta at beta=0.5 under the overlap rule, which is what ESA-ADB and Telemanom report. Telemanom's widely-quoted 0.71 is F0.5, not F1. point_adjusted_f1 is shown only to expose how much point adjustment inflates: TSB-AD (NeurIPS 2024) found a uniform random score ranks 26th of 32 detectors under it. Only labels whose ESA-ADB Category is 'Anomaly' count as positives; the 690 annotated rare *nominal* events do not.

telecom_ids.qml.framing: Architecture comparison, not a performance claim. The data is synthetic because no commercial-OK real attack corpus exists. Every published QML-IDS figure we could verify sits below a random forest on the same data, and arXiv:2512.05069 was withdrawn by its own authors for insufficient evaluation. Per-class F1 is the headline; aggregate accuracy is shown beside it because Engelen et al. (WTMC 2021) demonstrated it stays at 0.99 across a label correction that moved Bot F1 from 0.60 to 0.99.
